description: Einsteinium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Es and atomic number 99, and is a member of the actinide series and the seventh transuranium element. It is a soft, silvery, paramagnetic metal whose chemistry is typical of the late actinides with a preponderance of the +3 oxidation state. It was discovered in 1952 as a component of the debris from the first hydrogen bomb explosion.
uses: Due to the small amounts of einsteinium produced and the short half-life of its most common isotope, there are no practical applications for it except basic scientific research. Einsteinium was used to synthesize, for the first time, 17 atoms of the new element mendelevium in 1955.
characteristics: Einsteinium is a soft, silvery, paramagnetic metal with a density of 8.84 g/cm³ and a melting point of 860 °C. The high radioactivity of einsteinium-253 produces a visible glow and rapidly damages its crystalline metal lattice, with released heat of about 1,000 watts per gram. Like all synthetic transuranium elements, isotopes of einsteinium are very radioactive and are considered highly dangerous to health on ingestion.
